messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — I ran a paired A/B on the new v2-reranker (PTQ int8) where we explicitly compare a 'primed' input format vs the raw query (control). Seeing an inversion: NDCG@10 slightly up for primed on WebQA, but MRR drops on support queries. Thoughts?

sam: Can you paste the metrics? Which holdout and seed?

maria: Holdout: 2026-03-01 split (stratified by intent). Seed: 42. Small sample (5k pairs) for quick iteration. Results below.

jin: paste of quick table:

```
Dataset    | Arm     | NDCG@10 | MRR
---------- | ------- | ------- | -----
webqa      | control | 0.712   | 0.468
webqa      | primed  | 0.724   | 0.462
support    | control | 0.655   | 0.392
support    | primed  | 0.643   | 0.378
```

jin: Also ran a smaller check with HTML stripped vs raw and saw much of primed-penalty on support go away when HTML stripped.

maria: So candidate: priming helps when query needs better context but hurts when doc formatting noise interacts with tokenization. Possible PTQ tie-breaking shift exacerbates small score changes.

sam: Could this be tokenizer boundary + priming prefix causing different tokenization of short queries? That'd change internal normalization and candidate ties.

jin: Yep. I dumped tokenized lengths and top scores for a failing support example: primed input produced more subword splits in the first token and tied top-2 scores flipped ordering.

maria: Immediate next steps I propose:
- run 1k-sample paired debug with `--strip-html` and `--no-priming` to isolate formatting impact
- run PTQ replicate with different calibration seeds (2 seeds) to check quant instability
- add ranker-level tie-breaker deterministic fallback based on candidate id to measure effect

sam: Sounds good. Can you add the eval command you used?

maria: Command I used:
```
./eval_rerank --model models/v2-reranker-int8.ptq \\
  --holdout s3://bench/holdouts/2026-03-01.json \\
  --priming templates/short-priming.json \\
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 42 --out /tmp/ab_run.json
```

maria: I'll kick off the strip-html run and a 2nd PTQ seed tonight. @deploy-bot will post when jobs finish. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: Job 6212345699 started: eval_rerank (priming-control-arm, dataset=webqa+support, samples=5000).

jin: One more thought — add per-query delta histograms, not just aggregate. I bet the priming win is concentrated in long ambiguous queries.

maria: Agreed. I'll include per-query deltas in the next artifact and tag the slice for "short-support-html".
